Name: Global Water Watch
Description:
Global Water Watch, supported by Google.org and the Water, Peace, and Security Partnership, will provide free, globally accessible, near-real-time and high-resolution spatiotemporal information on the amount of water stored in reservoirs and the water level and flow in major river systems.

World Resources Institute, Deltares and World Wildlife Fund are partnering to create this data platform, which will house information on thousands of global reservoirs and major river systems. The platform uses Earth Observation (EO) algorithms, satellite data, artificial intelligence, cloud computing and machine learning to map dams and produce high-resolution spatiotemporal and granular (10m) information on the amount of water stored in reservoirs as well as water level and flow information in major river systems in near-real-time.

This data will help decision-makers respond quickly to extreme weather events, manage growing risks of climate change, make societies more climate resilient and preserve and restore our vital ecosystems and the many services they provide. National and subnational governments can use the data to manage water resources more sustainably, efficiently and equitably. Making this information publicly accessible will hold governments accountable for proper water stewardship and uncover water resource conditions in upstream states and nations, who may be reluctant to share data with downstream neighbors.

Commercial power now runs on proof.

Carbon borders are rising around the world's largest markets, and more are coming. Fuel buyers on the road, at sea and in the air price each batch on its carbon intensity. Tenders, banks and investors ask for your data before they accept your price. Prove your actual performance and you hold your margin, keep the order and keep your place in the market. Fall back on defaults and you pay a discount that never appears on an invoice, on every tonne, every batch, every contract.

Most companies fight this with spreadsheets, consultants and endless data requests. Cappi wins it with one move.

Your data goes in once. Product intelligence turns it into proof at the level your markets actually price, the product and the batch. From that single foundation, everything follows. CBAM proof that keeps exporters inside the world's most demanding supply chains and lets importers buy on actual figures, not punitive defaults. Batch Carbon Intelligence that makes every low-carbon fuel and feedstock batch count where it is priced, across road, shipping and aviation. Product sustainability that runs from carbon footprint to Digital Product Passport and ecodesign readiness. Reporting across CSRD, VSME, GRI and ISSB from the same verified data, so customers, tenders and investors get their answers in days, not quarters.

Then the same data works for you. It shows where the savings are, which market pays most for each batch, which suppliers strengthen your hand, what to fix first and what it returns. Sustainability stops being a reporting duty and becomes a decision you can price and act on.

Every figure traces to its source, and holds when it is challenged. In a market filling with fast, unverifiable numbers, that is the difference between a claim and an asset. Ask us to show you.

If you export, import, trade or supply where proof is priced, Cappi is built for you.

Cappi captures value from sustainability.

Name: CoAct Database
Description:
The CoAct Database is a global database that systematically maps cooperative climate initiatives (CCIs) and their contributions to climate and nature action. It is one of the most comprehensive datasets on non-state and subnational sustainability governance, capturing more than 1,000 initiatives and over 180,000 actor engagements across regions, sectors, and thematic areas.

CoAct documents how cities, regions, businesses, NGOs, and multi-stakeholder partnerships collaborate to accelerate climate mitigation, adaptation, and nature-positive action. For each initiative, it tracks actors, governance structures, commitments, activities, implementation status, and linkages to the SDGs. This enables comparative analysis of effectiveness, integrity, accountability, and the transformative potential of cooperative climate action.

The database underpins high-profile scientific and policy outputs, including contributions to the UNFCCC High-Level Champions’ Yearbook of Global Climate Action, global stocktake-relevant assessments, and peer-reviewed research on transnational climate governance. CoAct is developed and maintained through international collaborations, including the ACHIEVE, BioCAM4, and CAMDA projects.

Built to support researchers, policymakers, and practitioners, CoAct provides a robust evidence base for understanding how collective action beyond the state shapes climate and biodiversity outcomes—and how it can be strengthened to align with global climate goals.
Location: Nijmegen, Department Of Environment, Governance & Politics, Nijmegen School Of Management , Heyendaalseweg 141, Netherlands

governance · Geospatial climate risk modeling (remote sensing, LiDAR,

Name: ClimRisk
Description:
ClimRisk is a climate intelligence and risk analytics company focused on automating complex climate and sustainability workflows through its proprietary CRI Engine. We help organisations reduce the time, cost, and human effort required for climate risk assessment, ESG analysis, scenario modelling, and sustainability reporting.
Traditional climate and ESG projects often require large teams of specialists working for weeks or months across data collection, risk analysis, financial modelling, and disclosure preparation. ClimRisk was built to streamline and automate these workflows through a scalable, technology-driven approach.
Our platform combines climate science, financial analytics, and risk intelligence into a unified system that generates faster, more consistent, and decision-ready outputs for enterprises, financial institutions, consultants, and sustainability teams.
The CRI Engine supports climate-related financial analysis across physical and transition risks using globally recognised frameworks and scenarios such as TCFD, IFRS S2, NGFS pathways, and Net Zero 2050 models. The platform helps organisations evaluate climate exposure, operational vulnerabilities, portfolio risks, and potential financial impacts under different climate futures.
ClimRisk is not positioned as a traditional ESG reporting platform. Our focus is climate-financial intelligence and workflow automation that enables organisations to move beyond manual sustainability processes toward integrated, data-driven decision making.
By reducing dependency on large operational teams and accelerating complex analytical workflows, ClimRisk enables companies to improve reporting efficiency, strengthen strategic planning, and scale climate risk analysis more effectively.
